claims.text: The 5.00 SGD is already out of the rider's hands: EV-FARE-05067 records payment_status REFUNDED with refund_issued_sgd 5.00, and the trip record shows the fee reversed to the rider and withheld from the driver at 2026-09-13T10:46:10+08:00. Under POL-GEN-03 the driver's filing has to be read against that present payment state - NO_ACTION preserves the present state and never means 'restore a charge' - so the driver must affirmatively make out an entitlement to the whole 5.00 SGD before any money moves back to him. That is the frame for every point below.

The rider does not dispute the driver's contact: EV-CHAT-05067 carries three in-app messages from the driver (09:22:00, 09:25:30, 09:28:40) and EV-TRIP-05067 carries two in-app calls placed by the driver (09:24:10 and 09:27:20), all before the 09:30:10 cancellation. POL-NS-23's chat-and-call obligation is therefore met and the rider's case does not rest on it. What the rider's case rests on is this trip's timing, which the record cannot supply at all.

This booking has no scheduled pickup time: trip_record.scheduled_at is null in EV-TRIP-05067 and the derived driver_deadline is null with the reason 'on-demand trip: no scheduled time'. POL-NS-24 measures the driver's punctuality from the scheduled time plus 5 minutes, and its own note directs that where the record carries none and the deadline cannot be fixed, POL-GEN-26 applies; no artifact in this package can fix it. The timing fact that limb of the no-show framework needs is therefore not established on this record, and POL-GEN-26 sends the case to a human reviewer with the amount held - which leaves the 5.00 SGD refunded to the rider where it is, rather than paying it over to the driver on a deadline nobody can compute.

The no-show conclusion rests on the platform's wait timer and nothing else. EV-GPS-05067 carries an empty rider track (rider_track: []) and no rider-presence block, so no artifact places the rider anywhere; nothing in the record corroborates or contradicts her account that she was downstairs waiting, and the driver's own messages in EV-CHAT-05067 never once state that she was absent - his 09:25:30 message says he was himself 'waiting downstairs'. Whether the rider was at the pickup and available is a fact the record cannot establish either way, and POL-GEN-26 does not allow that gap to be filled by inference against her.

The rider's profile carries fraud_flags 3. I cite that field for one purpose only and for the rule that names it - POL-GEN-22, carried into no-shows by POL-NS-26 - and never as a fact about this trip (POL-GEN-01). Its effect is concrete: the confidence an AI ruling must reach on this dispute is 0.95, not the 'any confidence' that a 5.00 SGD no-show would otherwise bear. On a record whose only rider-side material is the rider's own uncorroborated note, and which cannot fix the trip's timing at all, a money ruling for the driver should not be issued at that bar; the fee should stay held for review.

EV-ADVIS-05067-01 is MISSING - no traffic record was attached for this trip - so it has no payload and an admissibility weight of 0.0, and I cite it at that weight and put no fact on it. Its absence means nothing on the record explains the 385 s the driver took between acceptance (09:15:20) and the arrival event (09:21:45) over a traced 1.444 km (EV-GPS-05067). Under POL-GEN-02 a MISSING artifact carries no fact and caps nothing by itself; under POL-GEN-26 a record with a hole this size in the trip's circumstances is one for review rather than for a money ruling.

The free wait was honoured and then some. The trip record puts the driver's arrival at 2026-09-13T09:21:45 +08:00 and the cancellation at 09:30:10, 505 seconds later; POL-NS-21's free wait of 300 s runs from that arrival, so it expired at 09:26:45 and the driver was entitled to cancel this trip as a rider no-show when he did.

The arrival POL-NS-21 depends on is not merely asserted, it is corroborated. The driver's own trace carries 29 fixes at a 30 s interval over 100% of the trip with a maximum gap of 30 s, and the nearest fix sits 1.81 m from the pickup point at 09:22:20, inside the 120 s window, reporting 6 m accuracy inside the 25 m filter and well inside the 50 m arrival radius for a STANDARD zone. The arrival check returns corroborated = true.

POL-NS-23 does not void this fee. The contact obligation has two limbs and the driver met both: three in-app messages at 09:22:00, 09:25:30 and 09:28:40, and two in-app calls at 09:24:10 and 09:27:20 (neither answered, ringing 30 s and 25 s), every one of them placed before trip_record.cancelled_at at 09:30:10. The voiding condition in POL-NS-23 is simply not triggered on this record.

The rider was on notice throughout the wait and chose not to answer. Each of the driver's messages was delivered and read — read receipts at 09:22:42, 09:25:37 and 09:29:09 — including the final 09:28:40 warning that the driver would cancel in a minute. A rider who reads three messages and declines to reply while the driver holds at the pickup is precisely the conduct the no-show fee exists to compensate.

The fee on the record is exactly the policy fee. Ev-FARE-05067 shows a single cancellation-fee line of 5.00 SGD charged at 09:30:14, reconciling to total_charged of 5.00 and matching POL-NS-22's 5.00 SGD no-show fee. Nothing on this record displaces the fee, so under POL-NS-22 the ruling is DRIVER_COMPENSATION, with amount_sgd and driver_compensation_sgd both carrying the same figure of 5.00.

NO_ACTION is party-relative and here it loses the driver the whole sum. The payments ledger already records payment_status REFUNDED with refund_issued_sgd of 5.00, and the trip record shows a fee_reversed event at 10:46:10 that refunded 5.00 to the rider and withheld it from the driver. Because the driver is the filer and the present state is a completed refund, NO_ACTION would simply leave that refund standing; only DRIVER_COMPENSATION of 5.00 restores the money the no-show fee gave him.

The reversal the rider relies on is not a finding against the driver. The platform's own event description records it as an 'interim reversal after a rider complaint ... pending review' — a payment action prompted by a complaint, not an adjudication on the merits. The merits are fixed by the arrival, wait and contact record, and that record satisfies every element POL-NS-22 requires before the fee transfers to the driver.

The rider's account is the only thing on her side and no artifact carries it. The statement that the driver 'never came to my block' is unsupported by any location evidence: the GPS artifact's rider_track is empty, while the driver's trace shows a stationary vehicle — zero speed at every fix — at the pickup point from 09:21:50 through 09:29:50, the whole of the wait. On this record the driver's account of arrival and waiting is corroborated and the rider's is not.

The rider's profile carries fraud_flags of 3, so under POL-GEN-22 the no-show ruling requires confidence of 0.95 and her assertions fall to be scrutinised accordingly — though that field never decides this trip. The driver's case clears that bar on the artifacts: every fact it needs is carried by a COMPLETE artifact at weight 1.0, and none of them is impaired.

POL-GEN-26 is not engaged, so there is no open question to escalate. The traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-05067-01 is MISSING — weight 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT — but no no-show rule needs a traffic advisory, and the facts the no-show rules do need (the driver's arrival, the elapsed free wait, the messages and calls before cancellation) are all established by COMPLETE artifacts at weight 1.0. The driver states the impairment plainly rather than presenting the absent artifact as clean.

POL-NS-24 gives the driver no trouble. It is the rider's right to cancel without charge when the driver is late for a scheduled pickup; this was an on-demand trip with no scheduled time at all (scheduled_at is null), the rider never cancelled, and the cancellation on this trip was the driver's after a completed free wait. Its goodwill-credit limb needs a driver who both failed to arrive and failed to attempt contact, and neither is true here.

The driver's claim text matches the record exactly rather than overstating it: he says he waited more than 8 minutes and made 3 messages and 2 calls, and the artifacts show 8 minutes 25 seconds of waiting, 3 messages and 2 calls, all before cancellation. Every element POL-NS-21, POL-NS-23 and POL-NS-22 requires is met, so the fee belongs with the driver and the interim refund should be undone by a DRIVER_COMPENSATION of 5.00.

ruling.explanation:
The no-show fee stands, and the 5.00 SGD already taken back from the driver must be returned to him.

To the driver: the record supports you on every element. EV-TRIP-05067 puts your arrival at the pickup (Block 680) at 09:21:45 and the cancellation at 09:30:10 — 505 seconds later. POL-NS-21's free wait of 300 seconds (5 minutes) runs from that arrival and expired at 09:26:45, so you were entitled to cancel this trip as a rider no-show when you did. Your arrival is not merely asserted: your own GPS trace (EV-GPS-05067, 29 fixes, 100% coverage, maximum gap 30 s, weight 1.0) shows the vehicle stationary at the pickup through the whole wait, with the nearest fix 1.81 m away at 09:22:20 reporting 6 m accuracy, inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius. Before cancelling you sent three in-app messages (09:22:00, 09:25:30, 09:28:40, all delivered and read) and placed two in-app calls (09:24:10, 09:27:20), so POL-NS-23's contact obligation is met and the fee is not voided. EV-FARE-05067 shows a single cancellation-fee line of exactly 5.00 SGD, which is POL-NS-22's fee.

To the rider: I have read the driver's filing against the present payment state, as POL-GEN-03 requires — the platform refunded 5.00 SGD to you and recovered it from the driver at 10:46:10 on an interim basis after your complaint. But because the fee was properly transferred to the driver, the 5.00 SGD moves back to him. The ruling is DRIVER_COMPENSATION, and both amount fields carry the same 5.00 SGD, which is the money this ruling moves — not a second payment.

On your arguments: I accept your filing-frame point and your concession that the driver's chat-and-call obligation under POL-NS-23 was met. I do not accept that the missing traffic advisory (EV-ADVIS-05067-01, weight 0.0) matters: no no-show rule needs a traffic advisory, so nothing turns on it. I do not accept that POL-NS-24 sends this case to a human reviewer. POL-NS-24 gives the rider a right to cancel without charge when the driver is late for a scheduled pickup; this was an on-demand booking (scheduled_at is null), you did not cancel, and the fee does not depend on the scheduled-time deadline, so there is no fact this case needs that the record cannot fix. POL-GEN-26 is therefore not engaged. Nor is your account that you were downstairs a fact the fee depends on: the no-show test reads the arrival event corroborated by the GPS trace, and both are in the record.

Your profile carries fraud_flags of 3, so POL-GEN-22 and POL-NS-26 require a confidence of 0.95. Every fact the driver's case needs is carried by a COMPLETE artifact at weight 1.0, and I am satisfied at that level.

No referral is owed: the fee charged was exactly the 5.00 SGD policy fee, so POL-NS-22's fee-amount referral does not fire; your no-show count on the profile is 1, below POL-NS-25's threshold of 3, so no repeat-no-show flag; and the driver both arrived and attempted contact, so POL-NS-24's goodwill credit does not arise.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties: on 13 Sep 2026 the platform charged the rider a 5.00 SGD no-show fee and then, after her complaint, reversed it to her and withheld it from the driver 'pending review'. The driver has filed asking for that sum back. On this record the fee was correctly charged and the driver is owed the 5.00 SGD.

The driver's arrival at Block 680 is established, not merely asserted. The trip record (EV-TRIP-05067, weight 1.0) puts arrival at 09:21:45, and the driver's GPS trace (EV-GPS-05067, weight 1.0) corroborates it: the nearest fix is 1.81 m from the pickup, reporting 6 m accuracy, inside the 50 m arrival radius for a STANDARD zone (POL-NS-21). Under POL-NS-21 the 300-second free wait runs from that arrival, scheduled trip or not, so it expired at 09:26:45; the cancellation at 09:30:10 came 505 seconds after arrival, i.e. after the free wait. The driver's contact obligation (POL-NS-23) was also met: three in-app messages (09:22:00, 09:25:30, 09:28:40) and two in-app calls (09:24:10, 09:27:20), every one before the 09:30:10 cancellation. The fare breakdown (EV-FARE-05067, weight 1.0) shows a single 5.00 SGD cancellation-fee line, matching POL-NS-22's fixed 5.00 SGD no-show fee. The fee therefore stands under POL-NS-22; because the platform has already moved 5.00 SGD back to the rider, that same 5.00 SGD is now returned to the driver: DRIVER_COMPENSATION, with amount_sgd and driver_compensation_sgd both 5.00.

The rider's points are answered. She is right, and it is not in dispute, that POL-NS-23's chat-and-call obligation was met. She is right that POL-GEN-03 reads the driver's filing against the present payment state, but the driver has affirmatively made out his entitlement to the whole 5.00 SGD, so that frame leaves the money with him rather than with the interim refund. Her argument that POL-NS-24 and POL-GEN-26 send this to a human reviewer fails: POL-NS-24 gives the rider a right to cancel without charge when the driver is late for a scheduled pickup, and she never cancelled; and the free wait on an on-demand trip runs from the driver's arrival (POL-NS-21, settled by Ryde on 14 Oct 2026), so no scheduled time is needed to decide this fee and POL-GEN-26 is not engaged. Her further argument that the record cannot place her at the pickup does not engage POL-GEN-26 either, because no rule makes the rider's own location an element of the fee; the fee turns on the driver's arrival, wait and contact, all established. Her statement that the driver 'never came to my block' is contradicted by the GPS trace, which shows the vehicle stationary at the pickup from 09:21:50 through 09:29:50, and nothing on the record corroborates her account (the rider track is empty). Finally, the rider's profile carries a fraud flag (3), which under POL-GEN-22 and POL-NS-26 raises the confidence this ruling needs to 0.95; every artifact carrying the deciding facts is COMPLETE at weight 1.0 (POL-GEN-02(2)), so the ruling is issued at exactly 0.95. No referral is produced: the fee charged (5.00 SGD) is exactly POL-NS-22's fee, so no fee-amount referral arises, and the rider's no-show count of 1, even adding this trip, stays below POL-NS-25's threshold of 3.

ruling.explanation:
Ruling for the driver: DRIVER_COMPENSATION of 5.00 SGD (the fare breakdown's fee_charged_sgd and driver_compensation_if_upheld_sgd, EV-FARE-05067). Because the driver filed against the refund already issued to the rider, both amount fields carry the same 5.00 SGD — the money the ruling moves back to the driver.

The driver's free wait was honoured (POL-NS-21). He arrived at the pickup at 09:21:45 and cancelled at 09:30:10 — 505 s later, against the 300 s free wait that ran from arrival and expired at 09:26:45 (trip_record.derived.free_wait, EV-TRIP-05067). POL-NS-21's start is settled at the driver's arrival whether or not the trip was scheduled (C2), so the absence of a scheduled time does not impair this limb. The arrival is not merely asserted: EV-GPS-05067 carries 29 fixes at 30 s, the vehicle stationary at the pickup from 09:21:50 to 09:29:50, the nearest fix 1.81 m from the point reporting 6 m accuracy, inside the 50 m STANDARD-zone arrival radius and corroborated = true.

The driver's contact obligation was met (POL-NS-23): three in-app messages at 09:22:00, 09:25:30 and 09:28:40 and two in-app calls at 09:24:10 and 09:27:20, all before the 09:30:10 cancellation, the messages delivered and read. POL-NS-23's voiding condition is not triggered, so no FULL_REFUND arises. The fee on the record is exactly the policy fee — a single 5.00 SGD cancellation line charged at 09:30:14 — so under POL-NS-22 the fee stands and the ruling is DRIVER_COMPENSATION of 5.00 SGD.

The rider's points are answered. (1) Her account that the driver 'never came to my block' is a counterparty statement carried by no artifact, while the driver's arrival is corroborated by the trace; on this record her version is uncorroborated. He then waited 505 seconds to the 09:30:10 cancellation, past POL-NS-21's 300-second free wait, which runs from arrival (C2, settled by Ryde). Before cancelling he sent three in-app messages (09:22:00, 09:25:30, 09:28:40, all delivered and read) and placed two in-app calls (09:24:10, 09:27:20), every one before cancellation, so POL-NS-23's chat-and-call obligation is met. The fee charged is exactly POL-NS-22's 5.00 SGD, so no fee-amount referral arises, and POL-NS-25's repeat-no-show flag does not fire (no_show_cancellations_30d 1, counting this trip 2, below 3).

The 5.00 SGD had been refunded to the rider and withheld from the driver at 10:46:10, but the platform's own event records that as an interim, complaint-driven reversal pending review (fee_reversed), not a finding on the merits. Because the driver filed, the question is only whether he is owed the money back; since the fee stands, the ruling is DRIVER_COMPENSATION of 5.00 SGD, with amount_sgd and driver_compensation_sgd both 5.00 (the same figure POL-GEN-03 requires).

The rider's points, answered. (1) POL-GEN-03's frame is right and I have applied it: the driver had to make out an entitlement, and he did. (2) POL-NS-23 is met, and the rider does not rely on it. (3) POL-NS-24 does not engage: it measures lateness from a scheduled pickup time plus 5 minutes, this was an on-demand booking with scheduled_at null, the rider never cancelled, and the wait and cancellation were the driver's after a completed free wait; POL-NS-21's clock runs from arrival whether or not the trip was scheduled, so the absent scheduled time is not a fact any operative rule needs and POL-GEN-26 is not triggered by it. (4) The empty rider_track is not an open question either: no no-show rule requires an independent finding that the rider was physically at the pickup, and the rider's account that the driver never came is resolved against her by POL-NS-21's corroborated arrival test. (5) The rider's profile carries fraud_flags 3, so POL-GEN-22 (via POL-NS-26) sets the bar at 0.95 rather than 'any confidence'; that bar is met, because every artifact carrying the deciding facts is COMPLETE at weight 1.0 and the confidence cap is therefore 1.0. The traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-05067-01 is absent (MISSING_ARTIFACT, weight 0.0) and carries no fact any no-show rule needs, so it caps nothing here.
